newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet Brent eases, but cash market firms.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet Brent eases, but cash market firms.

text.p: The North Sea physical market and Brent paper market headed in opposite directions on Friday, with firmer cash values failing to pull differentials for wet cargoes higher.
A wet Brent cargo loading June 16-18 traded at July Brent -49 cents on Friday morning, one cent down on a paper-related deal done on Thursday for a 12-14 cargo.
A June 13-15 cargo also changed hands on a dated-related basis on Thursday, while speculation that a June 19-21 cargo was also moved could not be confirmed.
According the original June Brent programme, three cargoes were due to be nominated loading dates between June 21-25 on Friday.
Other grades in the North Sea looked under pressure with unsold June barrels plentiful.
"We can see quite a few unsold June barrels in the North Sea at the moment," said one trader.
"There's still a bit of time for them to be placed, but you can see that physical cargoes are under pressure and differentials are coming off," he added.
